questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the intercept in a simple linear regression?

options.text: predicted value when the predictor is zero

questions.explanation: The intercept represents the expected outcome when the predictor is zero.

questions.prompt: Which assumption is NOT required for linear regression?
questions.explanation: Linear regression requires independence of errors, not of predictors.

questions.prompt: Which regularization method tends to set some coefficients exactly to zero?
questions.explanation: Lasso adds an L1 penalty that can shrink coefficients to zero.

questions.prompt: If the coefficient for X is 0.5 in a multiple regression model, what does this mean?

options.text: X increases Y by 0.5 units when all other predictors are zero
X increases Y by 0.5 units holding other predictors constant
Y decreases by 0.5 when X increases by one unit

questions.explanation: The coefficient indicates the change in Y per unit increase in X while other variables are held constant.

options.text: Residual plot shows a funnel shape

questions.explanation: A VIF above 10 signals high multicollinearity among predictors.

questions.prompt: Which metric is most appropriate for a regression problem with heteroskedastic errors?
questions.explanation: MAE is less sensitive to heteroskedasticity than squared-error metrics.
